title: A tiny load accumulates
hook: A 2 W standby all year. About how much energy?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert a small stated constant load into a multiday energy quantity.

misconception: A small wattage cannot accumulate a meaningful quantity over many days.
objective: Convert a small stated constant load into a multiday energy quantity.

claims.text: A constant illustrative 2W load runs for either 24h/day or 1h/day. Scaled model; Illustrative constant 2 W load, running for either 24 hours or 1 hour a day.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by this lesson's declared expressions; each card prints its working in plain words. At Days=365, A=17.52kWh and B=0.73kWh. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",2,24,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",2,"x"],1000]; x denotes Days. At x=365, A=17.52, B=0.73. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. Days slider now 5-400 in steps of 5 (365 is on the grid). The unused €0.30/kWh is taken out of the assumptions line. | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Own run: at 365 days A = 2 × 24 × 365 / 1000 = 17.52 kWh, B = 2 × 365 / 1000 = 0.73 kWh; readouts '2 W × 24 h × 365 days ÷ 1,000' / '2 W × 1 h × 365 days ÷ 1,000'. 365 is a slider stop (5 + 72 × 5). claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Same as lh-fixed-energy-charge c5: this is the unit definition (kWh = W × h ÷ 1000) and the model's arithmetic. formulaA = 2 × 24 × x ÷ 1000 and formulaB = 2 × x ÷ 1000; own run of resource-model.ts at 365 days gives 17.52 kWh and 0.73 kWh. Price × kWh appears in the assumptions (€0.30/kWh). Verified on the definition; energy.gov.au was not opened and is not relied on.
